In 2007, the [Football Association of Ireland](/wiki/Football_Association_of_Ireland "Football Association of Ireland") and [Scottish Football Association](/wiki/Scottish_Football_Association "Scottish Football Association") proposed the expansion of the tournament, which was later confirmed by the UEFA Executive Committee in September 2008.[[65]](#cite_note-65)[[66]](#cite_note-66) Out of the 54 member associations of UEFA, only three, including [England](/wiki/The_Football_Association "The Football Association") and [Germany](/wiki/German_Football_Association "German Football Association"), opposed the expansion.[[67]](#cite_note-platini-annoyed-67) On 28 May 2010, UEFA announced that [UEFA Euro 2016](/wiki/UEFA_Euro_2016 "UEFA Euro 2016") would be hosted by France. France beat bids of Turkey (7–6 in voting in the second voting round) and Italy, which had the fewest votes in the first voting round.[[68]](#cite_note-68) Euro 2016 was the first to have 24 teams in the finals.[[69]](#cite_note-69) This was the third time France have hosted the competition. Portugal, which qualified for the knockout phase despite finishing third in its group, went on to win the championship by defeating heavily favoured host team France 1–0 in the [final](/wiki/UEFA_Euro_2016_final "UEFA Euro 2016 final"), thanks to a goal from [Eder](/wiki/Eder_(footballer,_born_1987) "Eder (footballer, born 1987)") in the 109th minute. Cristiano Ronaldo, Portugal's world-renowned striker, came out of the game due to injury in the 25th minute. This was the first time Portugal won a major tournament.[[70]](#cite_note-70)

The **flag of the [U.S. state](/wiki/U.S._state "U.S. state") of [Missouri](/wiki/Missouri "Missouri")** was adopted on March 22, 1913, when governor [Elliot Woolfolk Major](/wiki/Elliot_Woolfolk_Major "Elliot Woolfolk Major") signed the State flag act making it official.[[1]](#cite_note-SOSMO-2) Its design consists of a [triband](/wiki/Triband_(flag) "Triband (flag)") of three equal horizontal stripes colored red, white, and blue, with the state [coat of arms](/wiki/Coat_of_arms "Coat of arms") in the center.

The design was created by [Mary Elizabeth Oliver](/wiki/Marie_Watkins_Oliver "Marie Watkins Oliver"), a Cape Girardeau native. The red and white stripes represent valor and purity, respectively. The blue stripe represents the permanency, vigilance, and justice of the state.

They returned along the same route in 1881.[[36]](#cite_note-Das1902-36)
